title: MIRACLE: II. Unveiling the multiphase gas interplay in the circumnuclear region of NGC 1365 via multicloud modeling
question: Characterize the multiphase gas (ionized atomic, warm and cold molecular) kinematics, morphology, physical conditions, and energetics in the circumnuclear region of NGC 1365 to understand AGN feedback and its impact on galaxy evolution.

data.angular_resolution: ~0.30" (0.35" x 0.31" final beam, corresponding to ~37 pc)
data.sensitivity: 1.5 mJy beam^-1 per ~8 km s^-1 channel

what.value: Mid-IR line ratio model predictions for AGN, SF galaxies, and shocks

evidence.loc: Resolved diagnostic diagrams for gas excitation
evidence.quote: we show the contours of line ratio model predictions for AGN (cite: Feltre+23), SF galaxies (cite: Gutkin2016), and shocks (cite: Alarie2019)

what.value: E-MILES stellar templates and broad [Fe II] emission template for MUSE pPXF continuum/BLR fitting

evidence.quote: Using the penalized PiXel-Fitting (pPXF, (cite: Cappellari2004)) code, we fit simultaneously the continuum and gas emission in the wavelength range 4800-9200 , convolving a linear combination of stellar templates (E-MILES; for details see (cite: Vazdekis2016)) with a Gaussian velocity distribution.

The BLR model consists of two independent components: a broad ($\sigma$>1000 km s$^{-1}$) Gaussian component for the broad Balmer lines (i.e., H$\alpha$ and H$\beta$) and a template of broad [Fe II] emission features by (cite: BorosonGreen1992).

what.value: BPASS v2.3 stellar population models used as incident spectra for SF photoionization grids

evidence.loc: Model grids of AGNs and SF
evidence.quote: As is described in (cite: Marconi+2024), the incident spectra for the SF model grids are stellar population models from BPASS v2.3 (cite: Byrne2022; Stanway&Eldridge2018) including binary stellar evolution.

recipe.goal: Reduce, align, reproject, and stitch multi-band datacubes (ALMA, MIRI, MUSE)
recipe.method: Image ALMA CO(3-2) cube in CASA and fit a 2D Gaussian to the central 2"x2" CO(3-2) flux map to define the nuclear astrometric reference; reduce MIRI MRS cubes with JWST pipeline v1.16.0, align MIRI and MUSE astrometry to the ALMA nuclear coordinates, reproject MIRI cubes to a common pixel grid, and stitch MIRI sub-band fluxes to Ch4 LONG.

recipe.goal: Fit emission lines spaxel-by-spaxel and generate moment maps across ALMA, MIRI, and MUSE
recipe.method: Fit ALMA CO(3-2) with a single Gaussian per spaxel; smooth MIRI cubes with a 1-pixel Gaussian kernel, subtract a linear local continuum, and fit 1-2 Gaussians per spaxel; Voronoi-bin MUSE cubes to S/N>=70, subtract stellar+BLR continuum using pPXF, and fit 1-3 Gaussians per spaxel.
key_parameters: KS test threshold p-value = 0.7 for MIRI (1-2 Gaussians) and p-value = 0.9 for MUSE (up to 3 Gaussians)
assumptions: Case-B hydrogen recombination ratio Halpha/Hbeta = 2.86 and G23 attenuation law for optical dust correction

recipe.goal: Construct resolved diagnostic diagrams and derive electron density maps and aperture values
recipe.method: Match FoV, pixel scale, and PSF across emission lines using WebbPSF deconvolution/convolution, compare mid-IR and optical BPT line ratios to AGN/SF/shock grids, and compute electron densities from [Ne V]24um/14um and [S II]6716/6731 using PyNeb.
key_parameters: 1.5" (~140 pc) radius aperture centered on the outflow region for integrated optical/mid-IR density comparison
assumptions: Electron temperature T_e = 10^4 K; metallicity cut Z > 0.006 for diagnostic grids

recipe.goal: Model optical and mid-IR line fluxes with HOMERUN and kinematic outflow structure with MOKA3D to derive outflow mass and energetics
recipe.method: Fit 60 optical+mid-IR emission lines in the 1.5" radius aperture using HOMERUN (combining dust-free AGN and dusty SF CLOUDY model grids) to derive ionized gas masses, and fit [Ne V]14um and [O III]5007A cubes with MOKA3D to obtain deprojected outflow velocities and energetics.
key_parameters: MOKA3D conical outflow maximum extension = 5 arcsec (~470 pc), PA = 235 deg; energetics radial extent Delta R = 284 pc (~3")
assumptions: Outflowing gas is fully ionized by the AGN (dust-free AGN clouds, dusty SF clouds with equal metallicity); constant flux density over time in each spaxel

answer_key.quantity: Electron density from [Ne V]24um/[Ne V]14um (1.5" radius outflow aperture)

evidence.quote: We derived the electron density from the [Ne V]$\lambda 24\mu\mathrm{m}$/[Ne V]$\lambda 14\mu\mathrm{m}$ line ratio, finding a median value of (750$\pm$440) cm$^{-3}$, consistent with previous estimates obtained from the optical [S II] doublet.
From the mid-IR [Ne V] line ratio, we estimate an electron density of (750$\pm$440) cm$^{-3}$, while from the [S II] lines we find a consistent value of (350$\pm$40) cm$^{-3}$.

answer_key.quantity: Electron density from [S II] doublet (1.5" radius outflow aperture)

evidence.quote: From the mid-IR [Ne V] line ratio, we estimate an electron density of (750$\pm$440) cm$^{-3}$, while from the [S II] lines we find a consistent value of (350$\pm$40) cm$^{-3}$.

answer_key.quantity: Median electron density log(n_e/cm^-3) across MIRI FoV from [Ne V] ratio

evidence.quote: Across the FoV, we estimate a median electron density of log($n_e$/cm$^{-3}$) = (2.7 $\pm$ 0.5), with a peak of log($n_e$/cm$^{-3}$)$\sim$3.5 at the nucleus.
The minimum of the curve is found for the minimum loss function of $\mathcal{L}_\mathrm{min}$ = 0.6, corresponding to 12+log(O/H) = 8.91.

answer_key.quantity: HOMERUN AGN component mean parameters (A_V, log(n_H/cm^-3), log(U))

evidence.quote: The data are best matched by a SF component with mean $\rm A_V$ = 3.3, $\rm log(n_H$ / cm$^{-3}$) = 1.3, and $\rm log(U)$ = -3.3 and an AGN component with mean $\rm A_V$ = 1.4, $\rm log(n_H$ / cm$^{-3}$) = 2.9, and $\rm log(U)$ = -1.4 (see Fig. 7).

answer_key.quantity: HOMERUN SF component mean parameters (A_V, log(n_H/cm^-3), log(U))

evidence.quote: The data are best matched by a SF component with mean $\rm A_V$ = 3.3, $\rm log(n_H$ / cm$^{-3}$) = 1.3, and $\rm log(U)$ = -3.3 and an AGN component with mean $\rm A_V$ = 1.4, $\rm log(n_H$ / cm$^{-3}$) = 2.9, and $\rm log(U)$ = -1.4 (see Fig. 7).

answer_key.quantity: Ionized outflow mass M_[Ne V] from HOMERUN

evidence.quote: We computed an outflow mass of $\rm M_{[Ne V]}$ = (109 $\pm$ 2) $\times$ 10$^{3}$ $\mathrm{M_\odot}$ and $\rm M_{[O III]}$ = (88 $\pm$ 9) $\times$ 10$^{3}$ $\mathrm{M_\odot}$ within the 1.5 radius aperture.

answer_key.quantity: Ionized outflow mass M_[O III] from HOMERUN

evidence.quote: We computed an outflow mass of $\rm M_{[Ne V]}$ = (109 $\pm$ 2) $\times$ 10$^{3}$ $\mathrm{M_\odot}$ and $\rm M_{[O III]}$ = (88 $\pm$ 9) $\times$ 10$^{3}$ $\mathrm{M_\odot}$ within the 1.5 radius aperture.

answer_key.quantity: Ionized outflow mass M_[Ne V] from classic/standard method

evidence.quote: Overall, with the classic method we find in the same spatial region $\rm M_{[Ne V]}$ = (2.6 $\pm$ 1.0) $\times$ 10$^{3}$ $\mathrm{M_\odot}$ and $\rm M_{[O III]}$ = (20 $\pm$ 7) $\times$ 10$^{4}$ $\mathrm{M_\odot}$.

answer_key.quantity: Ionized outflow mass M_[O III] from classic/standard method

answer_key.quantity: [Ne V]14um intrinsic outflow velocity v_out from MOKA3D

evidence.quote: We found that the best-fit parameters that reproduce the [Ne V]$\lambda 14\mu\mathrm{m}$ outflow features in NGC 1365 are $\beta$ = 82 $\pm$ 6$^{\circ}$, and v$_{\rm out}$ = 390 $\pm$ 35 km s$^{-1}$, consistent with the results in (cite: Marconcini2025_nat).

answer_key.quantity: [Ne V]14um outflow cone inclination beta from MOKA3D

evidence.quote: We found that the best-fit parameters that reproduce the [Ne V]$\lambda 14\mu\mathrm{m}$ outflow features in NGC 1365 are $\beta$ = 82 $\pm$ 6$^{\circ}$, and v$_{\rm out}$ = 390 $\pm$ 35 km s$^{-1}$, consistent with the results in (cite: Marconcini2025_nat).

answer_key.quantity: [O III]5007A intrinsic outflow velocity v_out from MOKA3D

evidence.quote: Moreover, we used $\mathrm{MOKA^{3D}}$ to fit the [O III]$\lambda 5007\text{\AA}$ spatially resolved emission assuming the same outflow geometry as for the [Ne V]$\lambda 14\mu\mathrm{m}$ emission and found $\beta$ = 84 $\pm$ 5$^{\circ}$, and v$_{\rm out}$ = 470 $\pm$ 40 km s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: [O III]5007A outflow cone inclination beta from MOKA3D

evidence.quote: Moreover, we used $\mathrm{MOKA^{3D}}$ to fit the [O III]$\lambda 5007\text{\AA}$ spatially resolved emission assuming the same outflow geometry as for the [Ne V]$\lambda 14\mu\mathrm{m}$ emission and found $\beta$ = 84 $\pm$ 5$^{\circ}$, and v$_{\rm out}$ = 470 $\pm$ 40 km s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Mass outflow rate Mdot_[Ne V] from HOMERUN+MOKA3D

evidence.quote: From HOMERUN, we calculated consistent mass outflow rates for [Ne V]$\lambda 14\mu\mathrm{m}$ and [O III]$\lambda 5007\text{\AA}$, namely $\dot{\rm M}_{[Ne~V]}$ = $\left(1.72~\pm~0.20\right)~\times~10^{-1}$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ and $\dot{\rm M}_{[O~III]}$ = $\left(1.68~\pm~0.31\right)~\times~10^{-1}$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$, respectively.

score_reason: All raw datasets (ALMA, JWST/MIRI, VLT/MUSE) and reduced MIRI cubes/moment maps are publicly archived, the MIRI stitching script is on GitHub, and key imaging, fitting, and photoionization grid parameters are well documented, though HOMERUN and MOKA3D codes are not publicly linked.
